title: Fields of definition of dynamical systems on $ mathbb{P}^{1}$. Improvements on a result of Silverman

predicted_errors.error_location: Theorem 2, immediately after the numbered equivalence
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Theorem 2 is corrupted by an inserted JPEG labeled “Figure 0.” In place of a mathematical condition, the theorem contains “(1) Diagram image” and “(2) Text crops (in reading order),” followed by a fragment beginning “where B is a Brauer–Severi curve...”. Thus neither condition (1) nor the asserted equivalence is actually stated. This is central to the paper because Theorems 3 and the later arguments explicitly rely on Theorem 2.

predicted_errors.error_location: Figures 1–5, at the locations where commutative/cartesian diagrams or mathematical displays are required
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Several large JPEG payloads have replaced required mathematical material. For example, immediately before Figure 1 the text says that after base change “we have a commutative diagram,” but no readable diagram is supplied; the same occurs before Figures 2–5. These figures do not provide the stated cartesian diagrams or the missing mathematical assertions needed by the surrounding proofs. Consequently, the arguments depending on those diagrams cannot be checked.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 4, paragraph after Figure 4 beginning “Furthermore, \(\mathcal{P}_\xi\) is a Brauer–Severi curve”
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper claims that the stack \(\mathcal{P}_\xi\) is a Brauer–Severi curve because its geometric base change is \(\mathbb P^1_{\overline K}/\operatorname{Aut}(\phi)\). But the preceding sentence identifies its geometric base change as the quotient stack \([\mathbb P^1_{\overline K}/\operatorname{Aut}(\phi)]\), which has nontrivial inertia at fixed points when the automorphism group is nontrivial. Such a quotient stack is not a Brauer–Severi curve (which is a scheme). The coarse moduli space \(P_\xi\), introduced later, is the object that can be a Brauer–Severi curve.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 4, paragraph beginning “Assume condition (2). The morphism \(\mathcal{P}_\xi \to P_\xi\) has degree \(d\) as well”
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: This confuses the coarse-moduli morphism with the dynamical endomorphism. The map \(\mathcal P_\xi\to P_\xi\) is the coarse-space map; geometrically it is \([\mathbb P^1/A]\to \mathbb P^1/A\), not the degree-\(d\) map induced by \(\phi\). It is generically degree one and is stacky over points with stabilizer. The subsequent inference for even \(d\) therefore does not follow from the stated morphism.

predicted_errors.error_location: Lemma 11 and its purported proof in Section 4
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Lemma 11 states substantial equivalences between descent, \(P_\xi(k_\xi)\), and \(\mathcal G_\xi(k_\xi)\). Its text then says “Proof. In general, there exists an extension \(k'/k_\xi\) of degree at most 2 with \(P_\xi(k')\ne\emptyset\), hence \(\xi\) descends to \(\mathbb P^1_{k'}\) by Lemma 11.” This does not prove either equivalence in Lemma 11 and invokes Lemma 11 itself as part of its own proof. It also only concerns an extension \(k'\), not the claimed rational points/descent over \(k_\xi\).

predicted_errors.error_location: Theorem 12 and the paragraphs immediately preceding and following it in Section 4
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Theorem 12 says that descent holds “if any of the following conditions holds,” but no conditions are listed. Surrounding paragraphs nevertheless refer to “condition (1),” “condition (2),” “condition (3),” and “condition (4).” The displayed proof begins “The second statement follows from the definition of \(\mathcal G_\xi\),” although the theorem as printed has no second statement, and is followed by the unrelated fragment “with the reduced structure.” Thus the theorem and its proof are incomplete and internally inconsistent.
